nodes.label: Prototype Domain Shape That Survived
nodes.rationale: model.service.ts settled on identity, classification, geometry, provenance and derivative-presence flags, with tags, groups and printer types as join tables resolved to sorted name lists. Lapidary keeps the shape and moves the join resolution behind repository traits. The bug not carried forward: listModels did SELECT * and filtered in TypeScript.

nodes.label: Three-Class Search Payload
nodes.rationale: One query returned matching models, creators with counts, and tags from matched models, with the header switching between POPULAR TAGS and TAGS & SUGGESTIONS. Tag counts came from a full GROUP BY on every keystroke, which tsvector plus pg_trgm and the 10k threshold replace — but the shape of the suggestion payload is right.

nodes.label: ingestMesh Ordering And Two Callers
nodes.rationale: The ingest primitive, called from the bulk folder scan and from the multipart upload branch. Tier 3 (compressed original) always first and unguarded, then Tier 2 (LOD plus metrics) through a 60 s sidecar; the thumbnail tier was explicitly out of scope and arrived later via its own route. The two callers diverge after it returns, and the divergence is not cosmetic.

nodes.label: The Prototype Never Hashed Anything
nodes.rationale: Grepping the four ingest services for hash|blake|sha256|checksum returns nothing — a direct divergence from 'hash first, always', not a variant of it. Duplicate detection happened a layer up by filename, and only on the scan path; the upload path had none. modelId was a fresh nanoid per call, never derived from content, so nothing was idempotent or resumable: identity must come from the content hash so a retried ingest is naturally recognized rather than accidentally re-run.

nodes.label: Orphaned Blob Leak On DB Failure
nodes.rationale: If ingestMesh wrote a blob and the following createModel threw, the scan path only incremented `skipped` and never unlinked it; the upload path had no catch at all, so it leaked and 500'd. Neither had a reaper. Blob writes need reconciling with the DB write — staged blob plus transactional commit, or an explicit reaper — because silent leaks are what 'we never delete user data implicitly' was written against, and never reclaiming orphaned data is just as much a problem to design out.

nodes.label: Measured And User-Typed Dimensions Shared Columns
nodes.rationale: The upload route wrote user-typed numbers into the same bbox_x/y/z columns a sidecar measurement fills, with no provenance marker. Either persist a provenance tag alongside every dimension triple or refuse to let a typed dimension land in measured columns at all — emphatically must not survive into Phase 1 in any form.

nodes.label: Vertex Clustering LOD On A 48-Cubed Grid
nodes.rationale: rust-mesh was dependency-free so it compiled offline in the container build — a constraint worth preserving. Vertex clustering is the right first LOD algorithm: single pass, no topology required, degrades gracefully on the malformed meshes real libraries contain. The 48 constant was tuned by eye and should become an L0/L1/L2 ladder.

nodes.label: Library Scan And The Debounce That Never Existed
nodes.rationale: A recursive synchronous walk-then-ingest pass bounded to 3 concurrent tasks, deduping by filename stem, with no watcher and no debounce at all — recording the absence is a real finding, not padding. Keep bounded concurrency and scan-as-an-explicit-action, which matches 'nothing happens implicitly'. Discard filename-stem dedup so same-named files in different folders do not silently lose one to unsorted walk order, and surface walk errors instead of letting them vanish.

nodes.label: Slicer Profile Parsing And The Curated Key Map
nodes.rationale: PrusaSlicer/Orca/SuperSlicer .ini and .json, chosen purely by extension. Section headers were recognized only well enough to be skipped, never tracked, so identically-named keys in different sections silently collide and the later one wins; no inheritance was implemented. The curated key map is the hard-won part and is the seed for lapidary-targets — captured before that work starts.

nodes.label: Explicitly Not Carried Forward
nodes.rationale: cache.service.ts and its Redis — the cache and the job queue are both Postgres; per-model procedural sample shapes in seed.ts, replaced by one real licence-clean example part; and `npm run dev` as the primary run path, replaced by podman compose up.
